title: Inject Current Date
summary: A Claude Code hook that tells the agent today's date, weekday and time zone on each prompt, so date math and changelog entries come out right.
description: Models often guess the date from their training data. This UserPromptSubmit hook reads the system clock and adds one line to every prompt: the weekday, the date in year-month-day form and your time zone.
That is enough for correct release notes, migration file names, license years and phrases like 'last Friday'. The hook never reads your prompt text and sends nothing anywhere.
useWhen: Write changelog entries with the real date
Name migration files with a timestamp prefix
Ask for deadlines relative to today
Update copyright years and expiry dates

hook.command: node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>{let j={};try{j=JSON.parse(d)}catch(e){}const n=new Date();const z=x=>String(x).padStart(2,'0');const day=n.toLocaleDateString('en-US',{weekday:'long'});console.log('Current date: '+day+', '+n.getFullYear()+'-'+z(n.getMonth()+1)+'-'+z(n.getDate())+' (time zone '+Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone+'). Use it for anything that depends on today.');process.exit(0)})"

example.prompt: Add a changelog entry for this release.
example.result: Claude receives 'Current date: Sunday, 2026-11-15 (time zone Europe/Berlin)' and writes the heading with that date.

faq.question: Which clock does it use?
faq.answer: The local clock of the machine running Claude Code, in that machine's time zone.

faq.question: Can I add the time of day?
faq.answer: Yes. Append n.toLocaleTimeString() to the printed text inside the command.

access: Prints one line of context; touches no files
